unverified: No claim failed the check (76 of 76 found); nothing was dropped for a failed check.

UNESCO: batuku is not on the UNESCO intangible heritage lists (only morna, 2019, for Cabo Verde). The national listing as Cape Verdean intangible heritage comes only from pt Wikipedia; the Nogueira 2011 thesis on the government portal (HTTP 503) and the Nogueira 2012 RBEC article (host unreachable) were not read, so its date is unknown.

The 1772 first mention rests on pt Wikipedia's quotation of the governor's ban, which speaks of 'zambunas'; the identification of zambuna with a batuku session is the article's own note. en Wikipedia says written records only from the 19th century.

Year of the Radio France/Ocora album Cape Verde: Batuque & Finaçon unknown: iTunes lists it twice (Nha Mita Pereira, release date 2001 but ℗ 2010; Ntóni Denti d'Oru, ℗ 2018); MusicBrainz search found nothing. Years left null.
Year of Bulimundo's Batuco: Wikipedia 1981, MusicBrainz 1982; 1981 used.
Year of Gil Semedo's Maria Júlia: Wikipedia gives the album Verdadi as 1996, iTunes as 1995; left null.
Lura's Di Korpu Ku Alma: pt Wikipedia 2004 (Lusáfrica, Paris), iTunes ℗ 2005; 2004 used.
Nha Nácia Gomi and Ntóni Denti d'Oru have no Wikipedia page in pt or en; their tie to batuku is only through album and track titles (Batuque & Finaçon; '(Finançon)').

Peak window 1995-2010 is a judgement from dated facts (revival 'in the nineties', Expo 92 and the 1995 Smithsonian festival, Pantera's 1993 nomination, field albums of 2003, the Pantera-generation albums of 2003-2008); no source states a peak.

Portugal 'later' from 1990 is a judgement: pt Wikipedia's photo caption shows batucadeiras in Damaia (Lisbon area) in the early 1990s, but that caption names no country, so the evidence used is Lura's Portuguese concert and the Orquestra de BatuKadeiras de Portugal.
